explain.1: Load PyTorch, so we can use torch.something.
explain.2: Load PyTorch's ready-made functions (softmax, cross_entropy) under the short name F.
explain.4: Our training text: the only thing your model will learn from.
explain.5: set() keeps each character once. sorted() puts them in order. This is the vocabulary.
explain.6: len() counts the characters in the vocabulary.
explain.7: An empty dictionary. It will hold pairs like 'h' → 3.
explain.8: Another empty dictionary, for the reverse: 3 → 'h'.
explain.9: enumerate() gives each character with its position: 0 and the 1st character, 1 and the 2nd, and so on.
explain.10: Save this pair in the dictionary: character → number.
explain.14: An empty list for every group's third-last letter.
explain.15: An empty list for every group's second-last letter.
explain.16: An empty list for every group's last letter.
explain.17: An empty list for every 'next character' (the right answers).
explain.18: Go through every 3-letter group in the text. Stop 3 early, so each group has a next letter.
explain.19: The group's third-last letter, as a number.
explain.22: The letter that really comes next: the right answer.
explain.23: Turn the list into a tensor, so PyTorch can use it.
explain.27: Show how many examples we have: 44 windows of 3 letters, each with the letter that comes next.
explain.30: Fix the random numbers, so you get the same result every time.
explain.31: The embedding table: a row of 2 random numbers for each of the 14 letters. Each row is that letter's embedding, shared by every position.
explain.32: The weights: for each next letter, 6 random weights, one for each of the 6 embedding numbers of a group.
explain.33: 14 × 2 = 28 embedding numbers, plus 6 × 14 = 84 weights: 112 numbers. Three small tables needed 588.
explain.36: The learning rate is 1 this time. 10 is too big for these numbers.
explain.37: Train 300 times: predict, measure, find directions, move.
explain.38: a) Predict, step 1: for every example, look up the 2 embedding numbers of each of its 3 letters and put them side by side: 6 embedding numbers.
explain.39: Step 2: multiply each of the 6 embedding numbers by its weight and add them up, for all 14 next letters at once.
explain.40: b) Measure, all in one call: for every example, softmax its scores into chances, take the right answer's chance, −log it, then average them all. One number: how wrong. Smaller is better.
explain.41: Clear the embedding table's old gradients.
explain.42: Clear the old gradients before finding new ones.
explain.43: c) Find directions: PyTorch works out every score's gradient (chance − goal, averaged over the examples) and puts them in .grad.
explain.44: d) Move: change every embedding number a little, against its gradient. The push reached them through the weights.
explain.45: d) Move: new score = old score − learning rate × gradient, for all 196 scores at once. .data means: change the numbers themselves, without PyTorch counting this move as part of the loss.
explain.46: % is the remainder. This is true at steps 0, 50, 100, … so we print every 50 steps.
explain.47: Show the step number and the loss.
explain.50: Fix the random numbers, so you get the same result every time.
explain.51: Start writing from “the”: the model needs 3 letters to begin.
explain.52: Write 40 more characters, one per round.
explain.53: Look up the embedding numbers of the last 3 letters written so far and put them side by side: 6 embedding numbers.
explain.54: Step 2: multiply each of the 6 embedding numbers by its weight and add them up, for all 14 next letters at once.
explain.55: Turn the added scores into chances.
explain.56: Spin the weighted wheel and take out the picked number.
explain.57: Add the picked letter to the text.
